title: Raster Graphics
body:
An image stored as a grid of pixels rather than as shapes to be drawn. The pixels live in
a **frame buffer**, a block of memory the display hardware reads out continuously, scan
line by scan line from top-left to bottom-right, redrawing the whole screen dozens of
times a second.

Because the buffer is just memory under [[Memory Mapping]], drawing is writing: setting a
pixel is a store to a computed address. On the Atari ST that address depends on the
resolution and how many bits each pixel takes, so the bit-twiddling is the work.

The hardware reading the buffer while you are writing it is the entire reason
[[Double Buffering]] and the [[VBL ISR]] exist.
